title: A queue item built on someone's claim is built unchecked
what: Before the build of a queue item whose failing case is a claim (a reviewer's, a scout's, the front's) and not a failing test or a recorded run, a cheap agent (scout or runner) reproduces the failing case on the live system: reproduced -> build; not reproduced -> no build, the item goes to the owner with what the check showed. Only when reproducing is cheap (a command, a read, a test); an expensive one (a paid run) stays the build's first step. Items whose failing case is a failing test or a recorded red run go as today.
why: Owner, verbatim, 24 Oct: "1. a" to: add the premise check only for items whose failing case is someone's claim, not a failing test. Live case: installed-relay-plugins-are-a-cached-copy-from-2 (a design reviewer's conditional claim, F12) went through build, review, 4 fixes and a hand-resolved merge conflict (about 200k agent tokens) before one 30-second command showed sessions load ~/relay/plugins directly; dropped with the owner's "1. a".
failing_case: 24 Oct: the plugin-cache item was built although its premise ("sessions load the stale copy") was never reproduced; a fresh `claude -p` session disproved it in 30 s after the build.
pass_cases: The skills say: an item whose failing case is a claim gets the reproduce step before its build; a non-reproduced claim stops the build and reaches the owner; an item with a failing test skips the step; relay queue add records which kind the failing case is.
where: rules/queue.md, relay queue add (a field saying whether the failing case is a failing test or a claim)
